En remplissant mes deux flasques souples: Filling my two soft flasks, I forgot one of them. An incredible stroke of luck: the Germans I had shared the bivouac with on the Kvalvika heights had picked it up on the way. Seeing my vest and the other, identical flask, we realised it was mine. Chance does things well.
Le plan prévoyait de dormir au bord du l: The plan was to sleep by the lake, but between the dense vegetation and the mosquitoes, there was no good spot to be found. So I set off again as it was getting late: a pass, a scree field, a second pass, then the descent to Horseid beach, reached very late but ahead of the route. A blessing in disguise: the spot was windy, but incredible.
Sur le papier, il suffisait de longer le: On paper, it was just a matter of following the fjord, as you would follow a lake in the Alps. In reality, it was the worst stretch of the whole traverse: mud, scree, invisible trail. Impossible to get lost since you had to stay along the fjord, but forcing a way through was exhausting, with countless U-turns to try another passage. The pace speaks for itself: barely more than 2 km/h moving over these kilometres.
J’avais perdu le chemin : il a fallu esc: I had lost the path: I had to climb a section of cliff with my bare hands, on soaking rock. Luckily I did not have to downclimb it, because on the way down I found the right trail again.
Au retour, dans une barre rocheuse, le s: On the way back, in a rock band, the ground starts shaking and stones come tumbling down above me. I press myself against the wall, arms over my head, and get hit by a stone the size of a billiard ball. More fear than harm, but I came down as fast as I could, frozen and a little shaken.
Une journée dantesque : la pluie ne s’ar: A dantesque day: the rain would not stop. I still decided to leave the tent for one last summit, but the trails had turned into torrents. A cave served as shelter, long enough to collect myself. Given what had happened to me the day before on Støvla, I chose safety: U-turn halfway up, the summit will wait. All that was left was to face the whims of the sky and run this last day.

Vers l’ouest : les falaises noires et le: Looking west: the black cliffs and the snowfields, under the clouds.
Depuis Napp, personne sur le sentier : d: From Napp, nobody on the trail: sheep, a few isolated houses, empty beaches. Offshore, a rock looks odd to me, so I take out the binoculars. It is a seal, only its head out of the water, motionless in the sun. I enjoy it for a long time: I am not sure I will see much wildlife here. The binoculars earned their place on the very first morning.
Nesland ressemble à un village fantôme :: Nesland looks like a ghost village: houses that look brand new, lawns mown to the millimetre, and nobody. It feels like a horror film, and yet the place is soothing. A resident finally appears, mowing, which reassures me. At the edge of the village, I sit in the sun and take out the Swiss army knife, from Vieux Campeur like almost all my gear, for a solo saucisson. My first Norwegian apéro.
Au pied du Volandstinden, de grands séch: At the foot of Volandstinden, big wooden racks where Norwegians dry cod in the open air: this is stockfish (tørrfisk), a Lofoten tradition for centuries. It is behind them that I hide my pack. Trail kit, poles in the quiver, music in my ears, and I take on the summit light for the first time on the trip.
Juste après les ponts de Fredvang, une a: Just after the Fredvang bridges, a sign announces a food truck a little further on the left. With all this sun, I am already looking forward to it: a hot dog, and a few words with tourists. When I arrive, it is closed. I sit at its tables anyway and take out my supplies, as planned at the start. To console myself, I finish the saucisson, and even take a waffle out of the pack.
Réveil tôt pour monter le Ryten en trail: Up early to run up Ryten, to the viewpoint over Kvalvika; higher up, everything is in the fog. I go back down to pack up camp with the Germans, and together we head for the beach, which is on the rest of the route: my first stretch of shared trail, and the last one too. On the beach, in full sun, we decide to rinse off. The water is icy, so cold that you do not feel the cold but a burn, the feet first. So we swim in intervals, to stay on the theme of effort: 5 minutes in the water, 5 minutes in a towel, in the sun and the wind. We come out with great photos and plenty of laughter.
De nouveau seul, j’arrive à un lac de mo: Alone again, I reach a mountain lake: for the first time, a landscape that recalls the Alps, a great cirque closed around the water. On a ridge, a dark shape moves. It takes me a long while with the binoculars to understand: it is a moose. I follow it with my eyes as it crosses the whole mountainside. Two animals in nine days is not a great score, but at least the seal has company.
Arrivé au point de vue sur la plage de B: Reaching the viewpoint over Bunes beach around 16:22, I think the day is almost over. It is only beginning. I first search on this side: too exposed to the wind. I go back down, pack on my back, then climb the other side. I put the pack down, go scouting, come back for it. 1 h 15 in total, just for a sheltered corner. And at the end, a ledge on the side of the cliff, just big enough for the tent, facing the beach. The search was worth it, but I no longer have the courage to climb Helvetestinden: with the pack, it already amounted to the elevation gain of a summit.
Au pied du Hermannsdalstinden, le plus g: At the foot of Hermannsdalstinden, the biggest summit of the trip: it was meant to be the biggest day. But the night lasted only two hours, and the fjord edge, between mud, invisible trail and sloping scree, had drained me. With altitude, the cold hits me, hands first. I give up and head to the Munkebu hut for a proper nap. I will more than make up for it the next day.
Une pizza et une fourchette achetées: A pizza, and a fork bought
Journée 100 % trail. Je descends vers Re: A 100% trail day. I go down to Reine by a path I had not planned, and treat myself to a pizza and a cocktail on a terrace. I take the time to think of my father, who sat in exactly the same spot the summer before. Before leaving, I buy a fork: I had lost mine, and eating freeze-dried meals without one was starting to become a sport. Then the 2,000 steps of Reinebringen await me.
Trempé par la descente sous la pluie bat: Soaked by the descent in the pouring rain, I settled below a cabin, 3 km from the harbour. I have two and a half days left: I will not move any more, the end will be done on trail from here. I am advised against the lake loop towards Å, so I stop at the Sørvågen grocery to stock up on sweets before tackling Andstabben.
L’Andstabben sous un ciel mitigé : roche: Andstabben under a mixed sky: slippery rock, many scrambling passages, and the brand-new Arc’teryx rain jacket finally paying for itself. At the summit, brushing my teeth facing the panorama, a few photos, then the descent to Å, the village with the shortest name in Norway. A plate of prawns awaits me there: well deserved.
